newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM gold firmer, other metals mostly weaker.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM gold firmer, other metals mostly weaker.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures ended firmer on Wednesday supported by moderate bargain-hunting buying while other precious metal futures ended weaker, weighed down by lower spot prices, traders said.
Activity was lacklustre partly ahead of a national holiday on Thursday.
Gold prices ranged from three to five yen per gram higher. Benchmark February was up four at 1,373 yen.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $349.70/350.00 at the Tokyo close, against $349.20/70 in New York on Tuesday.

"Gold futures are unlikely to slip sharply from the current levels, as individual investors may hunt for bargains on any price dip, taking a view that the yen will basically stay weak against the dollar," one analyst at a commodity broker said.
Activity in the bullion market was lacklustre. Traders expected spot gold to move within tight ranges until the Federal Open Market Committe (FOMC) meeting next week.

Platinum and palladium futures ended mostly weaker, but off early lows, as short-covering by private investors gathered force in line with the yen's slip and a rebound in bullion prices, the traders said.
"The palladium futures market lacked clear direction. The nervous trading is likely to continue until the timing of Russian exports to Japan becomes clear," one trader said.
Platinum futures ranged from 10 yen per gram lower to two yen firmer. Benchmark February was down one yen at 1,470 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from eight yen to 28 yen per gram lower. Most-active benchmark February was off 11 yen at 567 yen.
